column1: # INFRA-109 — the ONE list of symlink-following enumeration spellings.
# Read by BOTH enforcers: `.claude/hooks/bulk-edit-guard.sh` (the command, before it runs) and
# `scripts/harness/scan-symlink-following-enumeration.mjs` (the committed script). They used to hold
# the list twice, with each entry hand-rolling its own bound on what may stand between a command and
# its flag — and the three that had one were all different, so `rg`'s lazy unbounded form crossed
# `|`, `;` and `&&` alike while `find`'s two false negatives stood.
# TSV rather than JSON because one of the two readers is a PreToolUse hook: parsing JSON there means
# jq or python3 on every Write and Edit, and the format carries nothing that needs the extra grammar.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated:
#   id         the name this hazard is REPORTED under. Not derived from the columns beside it: `rg`
#              is known by its long form and `find` by its short one, and a derived id renamed a
#              hazard the moment the table gained a column
#   command    the program that must RECEIVE the option for the row to fire, matched by basename
#   short      a single letter, matched inside a short cluster (`-nL` carries `L`); `-` for none
#   long       comma-separated whole-word spellings, EACH with its own dashes because the two forms
#              are not interchangeable — find spells it `-follow`, rg spells it `--follow`; `-` for none
#   remedy     the safe sibling, stated at the finding, because a finding whose remedy is not stated
#              is one people work around
# Adding a spelling is ONE edit here. There is no per-entry bound to invent: what bounds the search
# is the STATEMENT, which both readers get from the same place.
id
find -L
column5: drop -L; plain find does not follow symlinks (measured)

column1: grep -R
column5: use -r, which does not dereference symlinks (measured)

column1: rg --follow
column5: drop --follow; rg does not follow, and honours .gitignore
